label: <DEL> step in sequences rich in p/b/s/f
explanation: Almost exclusively a delimiter-step unit: 97% of activation mass is at the <DEL> step (t == L), but it fires on only about 12% of <DEL> steps. Whether it fires, and how strongly, depends on which tokens the original sequence contained. It is graded by the count of p, b, s, f (and weakly j, a, z, 1), and h, x, d, c, o, i, 2 push it down. Longer sequences fire more often (rate at <DEL> grows with L). The top activations are sequences like b j p p s h y, s b r p p p s, b p b p, which are dense in p/b/s. Requiring 2 or more of {p,b,s,f} before <DEL> gets dev F1 0.45 (precision 0.36, recall 0.60, mass recall 0.72); the top activation quartile is 82% covered. This looks like a linear readout of the token-composition of the hidden state, so a hard count threshold misses both weak activations and inactive p/b/s-containing sequences. It essentially never fires during the original phase (2.7% of mass, weak) or the copy phase (<0.3%).
